zh.q: 岩层为什么会弯成波状？
zh.concl: 在强大的挤压力作用下，岩层发生塑性变形、产生一系列波状弯曲，叫作褶皱；背斜向上拱起、向斜向下弯曲（曲率符号一正一负）。
points: 岩层的变形和变位称为地质构造，褶皱和断层是常见的两种。
在地壳运动产生的强大挤压力作用下，岩层会发生塑性变形，产生一系列波状弯曲。
挤压越强、振幅越大：50 % → 100 % 时振幅 60 → 120 m，两处高差 120 → 240 m。

zh.q: 背斜和向斜，凭什么分得出来？
zh.concl: 背斜核部岩层老、两翼新；判背斜还是向斜，要把「向上拱 / 向下弯」的形态和核部与两翼的层序一起看。
points: 背斜岩层向上拱起、向斜向下弯曲，曲率符号一正一负。
但只看形态不够：剥蚀以后形态会倒置，得看层序。
判据是同一褶皱里核部与两翼比：轴部出露第 5 层、两翼第 6 层，层号小的是老——核部老、两翼新，所以这是背斜。

zh.q: 背斜明明是山，怎么成了谷？
zh.concl: 外力长期作用下会地形倒置：背斜顶部受张力、裂隙发育、被侵蚀成谷；向斜槽部受挤压、岩石致密、相对高耸成岭。
points: 背斜顶部因受张力产生裂隙，容易被侵蚀成谷地。
向斜槽部受挤压、岩石致密，不易被侵蚀，相对高耸形成山岭。
高差 dh 由正变负的那一刻就是倒置临界：4.0 Ma 两处等高，4.5 Ma 时背斜反而低 15 m。

zh.q: 岩层被切开以后，怎么错开？
zh.concl: 以水平位移为主的断层，使岩层在水平方向上被错断：同一层在断面两侧沿走向错开，错开量就是水平错距。
points: 当岩层受到的力超过所能承受的程度，岩层就会断裂并沿断裂面发生明显位移，称为断层。
断层的位移方向有水平和垂直两种；以水平方向为主时，岩层在水平方向上被错断。
错距是这把尺子：错距 100 → 200 m，同一层在断面两侧也错开 100 → 200 m。

zh.q: 岩块上下错动，会长出什么地貌？
zh.concl: 以垂直位移为主的断层：上升岩块常成为断块山或高地，下降岩块常形成谷地或低地；断层沿线岩石破碎，易发育成沟谷、河流。
points: 以垂直方向为主时，岩块交替升降：前块与后块上升、中间那块相对下降。
上升的岩块经风化侵蚀常成为断块山或高地（华山、庐山、泰山）；相对下降的岩块常形成谷地或低地（渭河平原、汾河谷地）。
落差就是断块山的相对高度：60 → 160 m。

zh.q: 考核：把断层调成水平位移并错开 ≥ 120 m，同时保持背斜处高于向斜
zh.concl: 水平位移的断层把岩层错断而不升降；倒置与否只看背斜轴部与向斜槽部的高差符号。
points: 先看「两侧岩层是错开还是升降」：错开＝水平位移，阶梯＝垂直位移。
再判背斜向斜：形态（拱 / 弯）+ 层序（核部老 / 新）。
倒置只改地表高低，不改构造——层序不变。

en.q: Why do rock layers bend into waves?
en.concl: Under powerful compressive force, rock layers deform plastically into a series of wavy bends called folds; anticlines arch up and synclines bend down (curvature signs opposite).
points: Deformation and displacement of rock layers are called geological structures; folds and faults are the two common kinds.
Under the powerful compressive force of crustal movement, rock layers deform plastically, producing a series of wavy bends.
The stronger the compression, the larger the amplitude: at 50 % → 100 % the amplitude goes 60 → 120 m and the height difference 120 → 240 m.

en.q: How can anticlines and synclines be told apart?
en.concl: In an anticline the core rocks are older and the limbs younger; to tell anticline from syncline, look at the shape (arched up / bent down) together with the core-versus-limb sequence.
points: Anticline layers arch upward and syncline layers bend downward, with opposite curvature signs.
But shape alone is not enough: after erosion the shape can be inverted, so look at the sequence.
The test compares the core and limbs of the same fold: layer 5 at the axis, layer 6 on the limbs, and the smaller number is older; core old, limbs young, so this is an anticline.

en.q: An anticline is clearly a hill. How does it become a valley?
en.concl: Under long-term external forces relief can invert: the anticline crest under tension fractures and erodes into a valley; the syncline trough under compression has dense rock and stands relatively high as a ridge.
points: The anticline crest develops fractures under tension and is easily eroded into a valley.
The syncline trough is compressed and its rock dense, resisting erosion, so it stands relatively high as a ridge.
The moment the height difference dh turns from positive to negative is the inversion threshold: at 4.0 Ma the two are level, and at 4.5 Ma the anticline is 15 m lower.

en.q: Once the layers are cut, how do they shift?
en.concl: A fault with mainly horizontal displacement offsets the layers horizontally: the same layer is shifted along strike on either side of the plane, by the horizontal offset.
points: When the force on rock layers exceeds what they can bear, they break and shift clearly along the fracture plane: this is a fault.
Fault displacement can be horizontal or vertical; when mainly horizontal, the layers are offset horizontally.
The offset is the ruler: offset 100 → 200 m, and the same layer is offset 100 → 200 m across the plane.

en.q: When blocks move up and down, what landforms grow?
en.concl: A fault with mainly vertical displacement: raised blocks often become fault-block mountains or highlands, dropped blocks valleys or lowlands; rock along the fault is broken and easily develops into ravines and rivers.
points: When mainly vertical, blocks rise and fall alternately: the front and back blocks rise and the middle one drops relatively.

Raised blocks, after weathering and erosion, often become fault-block mountains or highlands (Huashan, Lushan, Taishan); relatively dropped blocks often form valleys or lowlands (Weihe Plain, Fenhe Valley).
The throw is the relative height of the fault-block mountain: 60 → 160 m.

en.q: Check: set the fault to horizontal displacement with an offset of ≥ 120 m, while keeping the anticline higher than the syncline
en.concl: A horizontally displaced fault offsets layers without raising or lowering them; whether relief is inverted depends only on the sign of the height difference between anticline axis and syncline trough.
points: First check "are the layers on either side offset or stepped": offset = horizontal displacement, steps = vertical displacement.
Then judge anticline or syncline: shape (arched / bent) + sequence (core old / young).
Inversion changes only surface height, not the structure; the sequence stays the same.
